links.outcome: Radiologist AUROC with versus without AI assistance in mammography reading
links.effect: AUROC rose in junior residents (0.84 to 0.86; P=.38) and senior residents (0.85 to 0.88; P=.13). Senior residents approached consultant-level performance (difference 0.02; P=.051).
links.quote: With AI assistance, AUROC improved among junior residents (from 0.84 to 0.86; P=.38) and senior residents (from 0.85 to 0.88; P=.13), with senior residents approaching consultant-level performance (AUROC difference 0.02; P=.051).

links.outcome: Radiologist performance with AI in the intended workflow versus standalone AI performance
links.effect: Standalone AI AUROC 0.93 vs consultants 0.90 (P=.21). AI assistance improved resident AUROC and inter-reader agreement, mainly in dense breasts and less experienced readers.
links.quote: Diagnostic gains with AI were greatest in women with dense breasts and among less experienced radiologists.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests whether providing AI assistance (heatmaps and malignancy scores) versus unassisted interpretation alters radiologist diagnostic accuracy across different reader experience levels in a multi-reader multi-case design.
